newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends sharply higher on buying interest.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends sharply higher on buying interest.

text.p: NYMEX crude futures ended sharply higher on Friday, partly on short covering ahead of an annual industry event beginning Sunday and buying in the front calender spread.
"There was fund buying in the front month," said one floor trader, noting the April-May spread had emerged from a six cent contango to settle Friday at a nine cent backwardation.
April settled up 59 cents at $21.29 a barrel.
Traders also noted the expiry in the April crude options also buoyed the front month with buying seen in the $21.00 and $21.50 strikes.
Spread buying in favor of the front months also boosted refined products, with April heating oil ending up 1.11 cents at $55.33 a gallon.
The April-May carry narrowed to two cents from 36 cents on Thursday. Meanwhile, heating oil demand was seen firm near term with the new National Weather Service 6 to 10 day forecast.
The forecast starting March 20 called for much below normal temperatures in the northeastern United States, the largest heating oil market in the world.

"There was a lot of short covering in refined products," said Nauman Barakat, a trader with Prudential Securities in New York. "Gasoline is a seasonal play and once the market held at 64.00 cents it triggered some stops."
April gasoline settled up 1.54 cents at $65.77 a barrel.
With the approach of spring, dealers bought into an anticipated spring rally, which traditionaly occurs ahead of the summer driving season when gasoline peaks.
